question: A goods train, travelling at constant speed, crossed two persons walking in the same direction (as that of the train) in 11.6 seconds and 11.8 seconds, respectively. The first person was walking at 5.85 km/h, while the second was walking at 6.3 km/h. What was the speed of the train (in km/h)?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the 1st person = 5.85 km/h

Speed of the 2nd person = 6.3 km/h

Time taken to cross the 1st man by train = 11.6 sec

Time taken to cross the 2nd man by train = 11.8 sec

**Formula used:**

Distance = relative speed × time

**Calculation:**

Let the length of the train = LT

Speed of the train = ST

For the 1st person:

Distance = relative speed × time

⇒ LT = (ST - 5.85) × 11.6 ------- (1)

For the 2nd person:

Distance = relative speed × time

⇒ LT = (ST - 6.3) × 11.8 ------- (1)

From eq.(1) and (2)

⇒ (ST - 5.85) × 11.6 = (ST - 6.3) × 11.8

⇒ (ST - 5.85) × 58 = (ST - 6.3) × 59

⇒ 58ST - 59ST = (5.85 × 58) - (6.3 × 59)

⇒ - ST = 339.3 - 371.7

⇒ ST = 32.4 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 32.4 km/h. **
